name: zipbox

modes.label: Per-second fixed VM sizes
modes.note: Published hourly list rates (zipbox.ai/pricing and /docs/pricing, 2026-09-28): Tiny $0.0068, Small $0.0137, Medium $0.0274, Large $0.0548 per hour, "Machine time metered by the second while running"; the "~$5/$10/$20/$40 /mo" always-on figures are just hourly x ~730, not a cap or discount. "Paused boxes cost $0". Larger sizes on request ("Bigger machines on request: contact us", pricing); the API names tiers xs to xxl but publishes no xl/xxl size or price. Rates re-checked 2026-11-08: unchanged.
modes.note (append): Platform-proxied LLM calls billed at provider cost + 3%; bring-your-own subscription bills machine time only. Stopped = disk archived to cold storage, meter stops; start restores the same disk (no memory state).

plans.name: Prepaid pay as you go
plans.note: Prepaid credit, no subscription; the $25 signup credit needs a one-time $5 top-up; no general minimum top-up and no credit expiry rule is published (docs/pricing, docs/faq, 2026-11-08); a positive balance is required to boot. At $0 balance a 1-hour grace window, then running boxes are paused (archived). Concurrency limit not published.

features.ip_note: Egress/IP and proxy options not documented; each microVM has its own public hostname and network.

caveats: Displayed $5/$10/$20/$40 monthly equivalents are not stated as billing caps or always-on discounts; use hourly rates.
Stop (formerly pause) saves the whole disk at $0; no memory state, no named snapshots or templates (docs/lifecycle).

Account cap: 250 machine names for life, deleted boxes included; support raises it. No limit on boxes running at once is published (null = unknown, not unlimited). Max session length, egress charge and public IPv4 pricing are not published. SSH is IPv6-only.
LLM/API calls using platform keys draw the same credit balance and are additional; own model subscriptions separate.

Signup credit re-verified 2026-10-14: "Every new account gets $25 in credit after a one-time $5 top-up (card or crypto) - one grant per person, and it lands in the same balance as a top-up" (docs/pricing). The $25 is no longer free on signup: it unlocks only after paying a one-time $5 top-up (the $5 itself stays spendable balance), and it can be skipped. Credits are prepaid and non-refundable.
No independent runtime/account test or performance measurement performed.
No idle auto-stop: "Nothing stops, pauses or deletes a box on a clock" (docs/lifecycle); the only automatic stop is 1 hour after the balance hits $0.

Features check 2026-10-14: desktop true. docs/skills documents "zipbox-desktop Drives the box's X11 desktop - windows, mouse, keyboard - the same session you watch from the right rail" and the homepage calls the box "A web operating system with a browser, a file manager, ..." (ZipOS); the 2026-09-28 'no desktop documented' note is superseded. Fork/clone of a box and Docker-inside are undocumented (null). Firecracker ("Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM", docs/security) => no /dev/kvm in guests (firecracker tests/integration_tests/security/test_nv.py).

Since 2026-10-21: public REST API (OpenAPI 3.1), TypeScript/Python/Go/Rust SDKs, CLI and hosted MCP create, start, stop, resize and delete boxes and run commands, files, terminals, previews and desktop screenshots (docs/api). No agent prompt/steer API.
Inbound: preview URLs give any port a public HTTPS URL with no documented sign-in; custom domains via Caddy (30 records per apex, docs/domains); Tailscale private mode closes public routes.

fleet.verification: The $25 signup credit unlocks only after a one-time $5 top-up (card or crypto), one grant per person (docs/pricing, docs/faq, 2026-10-14); positive balance to boot. A card on file is not required ("any balance above $0 boots any machine, with or without a card on file", docs/faq); top-ups by card/crypto via Stripe and saved card for auto-refill.
fleet.notes: An account holds 250 machine names for life: running, stopped and deleted boxes all count (docs/machine-limit). Raise by email to support@tribes.xyz. No limit on boxes running at once is published. API: 600 control-plane requests per minute per key; 32 concurrent commands per box.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: there are no templates or snapshots, because a box is its environment.
snapshot_auto.note: Stop (formerly "pause") archives the disk; no automatic snapshots.

guest_firewall.quote: Inside the box you are root.
guest_firewall.note: Not published: no zipbox page mentions nftables, iptables or a firewall inside the box (docs/agents, docs/security, llms-full.txt checked 2026-11-08). Root plus an own kernel makes it likely, but likely is not a source.

browser.quote: Every box has a full desktop with a browser.
browser.note: docs/skills also lists zipbox-browser: headless Google Chrome via Playwright CLI.

ssh.note: SSH with your own public key from Settings; the CLI page says "Your network needs IPv6; if it has none, use `zipbox shell`, which runs over HTTPS."

secret_proxy.quote: Zipbox's rule is simple: the real key never enters the machine. The box holds a public placeholder and sends it like a normal key. After the request leaves the box, the host swaps in the real key.
secret_proxy.note: Arbitrary user-added hosts (up to 8 hosts per key, 20 keys per store), per machine or all machines; placeholder slot types: Bearer token, custom header, URL query parameter, Basic Auth, URL path, JSON body field. Mechanism: /etc/hosts points the host at 172.16.0.1, TLS terminated by a host CA the box trusts. Plus platform-billed included services (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, xAI, Tavily, Apify, etc.). HTTPS only; non-HTTP (DB URLs etc.) must use 'Key = value' env vars that do enter the box. Root in the box can remove /etc/hosts lines to bypass (then it just lacks the key).

image_oci.quote: Everything else - machine size, a GitHub repository to clone, LLM billing, SSH keys - is on the same form, and the defaults are fine.
image_oci.note: The create-sandbox form's full option list (name, agent, size, GitHub repo, LLM billing, SSH keys) has no custom Docker/OCI image field; not offered.

docker_inside.quote: Inside the box you are root. Agents can install packages, bind ports, rewrite configs, and run overnight jobs.
docker_inside.note: Not published: no zipbox page mentions Docker, dockerd, podman or containers inside a box (full llms-full.txt, docs/agents, docs/faq, docs/security searched 2026-11-08). The previous true was derived from root + own kernel, with no provider quote.

anti_bot.quote: zipbox-browser Headless Google Chrome via Playwright CLI for JS-heavy pages, clicks, screenshots, and PDFs.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - the browser skill is plain headless/streamed Chrome via Playwright, no stealth/fingerprint-evasion features documented.

captcha_solving.quote: zipbox-browser Headless Google Chrome via Playwright CLI for JS-heavy pages, clicks, screenshots, and PDFs.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no CAPTCHA-solving service or skill is documented anywhere in the docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM: a small virtual machine with its own Linux kernel, filesystem, public hostname, and network.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: standard cloud/datacenter hosting infrastructure; no residential/mobile proxy or egress-IP product is offered.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: there are no templates or snapshots, because a box is its environment.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Stop archives the whole disk to cold storage at $0 and start brings it back (persist_scope whole). No named snapshot to restore or start a new box from.

fork.quote: there are no templates or snapshots, because a box is its environment.
fork.note: The API lists create, list, start, stop, restart, resize and delete; no clone or fork is documented.

fork_running.quote: The card's ⋮ menu holds the actions: Open terminal, Copy domain, Copy email, Upgrade tier, Pause, Reboot, Delete.
fork_running.note: No fork feature exists at all (see fork), so cloning a running machine is not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Paused - the disk is archived and the meter stops ($0); Restore boots the same disk on fresh hardware
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork feature exists, and even pause/restore preserves disk only, not running memory; not offered.

wake_on_request.quote: Paused - the disk is archived and the meter stops ($0); Restore boots the same disk on fresh hardware
wake_on_request.note: Restore is a manual dashboard action; no documented mechanism wakes a paused box automatically when an inbound request arrives.

volume_attach.quote: Tiny 1 vCPU · 2 GB RAM · 20 GB disk $0.0068 /hr ... Large 6 vCPU · 16 GB RAM · 320 GB disk $0.0548 /hr
volume_attach.note: Disk is a fixed part of each size tier; no separate attachable-volume feature is documented.

volume_shared.quote: Tiny 1 vCPU · 2 GB RAM · 20 GB disk $0.0068 /hr ... Large 6 vCPU · 16 GB RAM · 320 GB disk $0.0548 /hr
volume_shared.note: No volumes feature exists at all (see volume_attach), so a shared volume across machines is not offered.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Nothing stops, pauses or deletes a box on a clock.
auto_stop_idle.note: No idle stop. The only automatic stop is 1 hour after the balance hits $0 (docs/pricing).

live_resize.quote: A running box is archived and restored into the new size; its files come with it.
live_resize.note: Resize (tiers xs, s, m, l, xl, xxl) works on a running box but archives and restores it, so processes restart. Upgrades only.

harness_api.quote: Boxes: create, list, start, stop, restart, resize and delete them.
harness_api.note: Since 2026-10-21 the API drives boxes, commands, files, terminals, previews and desktop screenshots. It has no agent prompt, steer or event API: you start the agent CLI as a command and read its output yourself.

own_agent_api.quote: Zipbox is agent-agnostic: pick the assistant you already use.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Zipbox hosts third-party coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) rather than shipping its own task/browser/computer-use agent with an API.

mcp_server.quote: Hosted MCP server (OAuth, or Authorization: Bearer zb_…)
mcp_server.note: Launched 2026-10-21 with a REST API (OpenAPI 3.1), TypeScript/Python/Go/Rust SDKs and a CLI (https://zipbox.ai/blog/zipbox-api-sdks-mcp-cli). MCP endpoint: https://mcp.zipbox.ai.

lang_node.quote: Claude Code - Anthropic Codex - OpenAI ... opencode - Open-source terminal agent Cline - Open-source coding agent
lang_node.note: derived: Claude Code, opencode and Cline are Node.js-based CLIs shipped pre-installed and already running on boot, so a Node.js runtime must be present out of the box.

public_ipv4.quote: SSH reaches boxes over IPv6 only - on an IPv4-only network the terminal in the browser still works, but ssh will not connect.
public_ipv4.note: No public IPv4 per machine; the box's own network is IPv6 (inbound HTTPS is proxied via Caddy/hostname rather than a raw public IPv4).

ingress_rules.quote: Only then does the host drop the box's public routes.
ingress_rules.how: join the box to your tailnet in private mode; only your tailnet devices reach it
ingress_rules.note: Public preview URLs (https://<label>.<box host>) have no documented sign-in or IP allowlist; private mode is all-or-nothing per box.

egress_allowlist.quote: No proxy settings. Do not export HTTP_PROXY.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side outbound allow/deny list or no-internet mode is documented; the only edge control is credential swapping for known API hosts, not egress filtering.

egress_http_rules.quote: A placeholder only works on the host its key belongs to. Sent anywhere else - an attacker, a log, a paste bin - it is a meaningless string.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented; not offered.

static_egress_ip.quote: Paused - the disk is archived and the meter stops ($0); Restore boots the same disk on fresh hardware
static_egress_ip.note: Restore boots the disk on fresh hardware, implying network/IP is not preserved across pause/restore; no fixed outbound IP is documented.

gpu.quote: Larger sizes (XL / XXL) appear as coming soon on the pricing page - email support@tribes.xyz when you need them.
gpu.note: Only CPU sizes (Tiny/Small/Medium/Large, with XL/XXL CPU tiers coming soon) are listed; no GPU option exists.

windows.note: The product's structured data declares Linux (and Web) only.

macos.note: Linux-only Firecracker microVMs; macOS is not offered.

arm64.quote: Tiny 1 vCPU · 2 GB RAM · 20 GB disk $0.0068 /hr ... Large 6 vCPU · 16 GB RAM · 320 GB disk $0.0548 /hr
arm64.note: No architecture choice is published for the machine sizes; no ARM option is documented.

self_host.quote: zipbox: a cloud computer for your AI agent
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Zipbox is a hosted SaaS run by Tribes, Inc., with no self-hosted deployment option documented.

byoc.quote: zipbox: a cloud computer for your AI agent
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no bring-your-own-cloud deployment is documented; boxes run on Zipbox's own infrastructure.

open_source.quote: zipbox: a cloud computer for your AI agent
open_source.note: Zipbox is a commercial SaaS product from Tribes, Inc.; no OSI license for the core platform is published (the coding agents it hosts, e.g. opencode, are separately open source, but that is not the same product).

soc2.quote: Every section below is one of those walls. Hardware isolation ... Sessions without passwords ... Keys are injected, never stored ... Report a vulnerability
soc2.note: The full Security doc covers isolation, sessions, key handling, wallets, and data retention but never mentions SOC 2 or any compliance attestation.

hipaa.quote: Every section below is one of those walls. Hardware isolation ... Sessions without passwords ... Keys are injected, never stored ... Report a vulnerability
hipaa.note: No HIPAA-eligibility or BAA offering is mentioned anywhere in the security or pricing docs.

sso.quote: Open the dashboard and sign in with an email address or a crypto wallet.
sso.note: Sign-in is email, crypto wallet, or social login; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM: a small virtual machine with its own Linux kernel, filesystem, public hostname, and network.
eu_data_residency.note: No region selection or EU data-residency option is published anywhere in the docs or pricing pages.

max_session_h.quote: Prepaid credits - no subscription Machine time metered by the second while running Paused boxes cost $0
max_session_h.note: No maximum session/run duration is documented anywhere in pricing, security, or lifecycle docs; a box runs until paused, rebooted, or deleted, or the credit balance hits $0.

nested_virt.quote: Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM - the virtualization technology that runs AWS Lambda. Unlike a container, which shares its host's kernel with every other container on the machine, each box boots its own Linux kernel under hardware virtualization (KVM), behind a deliberately tiny virtual device surface.
nested_virt.note: Zipbox's own security page confirms each box is a Firecracker/KVM microVM with a deliberately minimal virtual device surface; Firecracker does not expose /dev/kvm or virtualization extensions to the guest (Firecracker's own test suite, tests/integration_tests/security/test_nv.py, explicitly asserts nested virtualization is disabled inside its microVMs). No zipbox page advertises nested virtualization or /dev/kvm-in-guest support. Confirms the recorded 'no'.

lang_python.quote: When python wasn’t on PATH, Codex noticed, switched to python3, and finished the fix. Ran python3 -m unittest -v: test_even_list ... ok test_odd_list ... ok
lang_python.note: Captured live session on a boot machine shows python3 present and running unittest successfully out of the box (python, without the 3 suffix, was not on PATH in that session).

usage_api.quote: plus reading your balance and usage.
usage_api.note: The API reads balance and usage; the docs do not say if usage is per box. The dashboard Usage page itemizes machine time per box.

persist_scope.quote: the box bills nothing while stopped.
persist_scope.note: Stop archives the whole disk to cold storage; start restores it, "in seconds" when the last host still holds the disk, else "under a minute for a Tiny box, minutes for larger disks". Deleted boxes keep a recoverable copy for 30 days.

custom_image.quote: Everything else - machine size, a GitHub repository to clone, LLM billing, SSH keys - is on the same form, and the defaults are fine.
custom_image.note: Create form offers name, agent, size, GitHub repo, LLM billing and SSH keys only; boxes boot from Zipbox's own pre-warmed image, with no user-supplied/custom image option documented (same basis as image_oci). Lifecycle docs (2026-11-08): "there are no templates or snapshots, because a box is its environment."

agent_harnesses.quote: Pi, Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Muse Spark, Hermes, OpenClaw, opencode, Cline, Cursor CLI, Command Code, Amp and Herdr today, plus plain bash. Pick one at boot; each runs with its vendor’s own defaults.
agent_harnesses.note: 13 harnesses selectable at boot (Herdr is a runtime that hosts other agents, per docs/get-started); Cursor CLI, Command Code and Amp use your own vendor account.

desktop.quote: zipbox-desktop Drives the box's X11 desktop - windows, mouse, keyboard - the same session you watch from the right rail.
desktop.note: Each box runs an X11 desktop (ZipOS: "A web operating system with a browser, a file manager, ...", homepage) streamed to the dashboard's right rail ("the remote desktop", docs/terminal-footer), which you can watch or take over; the agent drives it through the zipbox-desktop skill. Since 2026-10-21 the API also returns desktop screenshots ("screenshot() returns a PNG of the box's desktop", llms.txt); no click/type input API is documented.

private_network.quote: Put a box on your own tailnet with a one-off auth key sealed on your machine,
private_network.note: The box shows up as a device on your tailnet. Private mode then drops the box public routes.

locations_quote: Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM: a small virtual machine with its own Linux kernel, filesystem, public hostname, and network.
